A rod of length L has non-uniform linear mass

density given by $ρ$(x) = $a+b\left (\frac{x}{L}\right )^{2}$

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$ρ$ = a + b$\left (\frac{x}{L}\right )^{2}$

dm = $ρ$dx = $\left (a+b\frac{x^{2}}{L^{2}}\right )dx$

M = $\int dm$ = $\int\limits _{0}^{L}\left (a+b\frac{x^{2}}{L^{2}}\right )dx$

$X_{$com} = $\frac{\int xdm}{\int dm}$

= $\frac{\int\limits _{0}^{L}\left (a+b\frac{x2}{L2}\right )xdx}{\int\limits _{0}^{L}\left (a+b\frac{x2}{L2}\right )dx}$

= $\frac{\frac{aL2}{2}+\frac{b}{L2}.\frac{L4}{4}}{aL+\frac{b}{L2}.\frac{L3}{3}}$

= $\frac{\left (\frac{4a+2a}{8}\right )L}{\left (\frac{3a+b}{3}\right )}$

= $\frac{3}{4}\left (\frac{2a+b}{3a+b}\right )L$

text:
An electron gun is placed inside a long solenoid
of radius R on its axis. The solenoid has n
turns/length and carries a current I. The
electron gun shoots an electron along the radius
of the solenoid with speed v. If the electron
does not hit the surface of the solenoid,
maximum possible value of v is (all symbols
have their standard meaning) :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Inside the long solenoid the field is uniform and along the axis: $B=μ_{0}nI$.

The electron is fired along a radius, perpendicular to $⃗{B}$, so it moves in a circle in the cross-sectional plane with radius

$r=\dfrac{mv}{eB}$

The circle starts at the axis, so the axis is a point on the circle; the point of the path farthest from the axis is diametrically opposite to it, at a distance $2r$.

The electron does not hit the surface if $2r\leq R$:

$\dfrac{2mv}{eB}\leq R\Rightarrow v\leq \dfrac{eBR}{2m}=\dfrac{eμ_{0}nIR}{2m}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text:
A small circular loop of conducting wire has
radius a and carries current I. It is placed in a
uniform magnetic field B perpendicular to its
plane such that when rotated slightly about its
diameter and released, it starts performing
simple harmonic motion of time period T. If the
mass of the loop is m then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The loop has magnetic moment $μ=Iπa^{2}$, along $⃗{B}$ in equilibrium. Turned through a small angle $θ$ about a diameter, it feels a restoring torque

$τ=-μB\sin θ\approx -Iπa^{2}Bθ$

The moment of inertia of a ring about a diameter is $\dfrac{ma^{2}}{2}$, so

$\dfrac{ma^{2}}{2}α=-Iπa^{2}Bθ\Rightarrow α=-\dfrac{2πIB}{m}θ$

This is simple harmonic motion with $ω^{2}=\dfrac{2πIB}{m}$:

$T=\dfrac{2π}{ω}=2π\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{2πIB}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{4π^{2}m}{2πIB}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{2πm}{IB}}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text:
There is a small source of light at some depth
below the surface of water (refractive
index = $\frac{4}{3}$) in a tank of large cross sectional
surface area. Neglecting any reflection from the
bottom and absorption by water, percentage of
light that emerges out of surface is (nearly) :

[Use the fact that surface area of a spherical cap
of height h and radius of curvature r is 2$π$rh]:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Light from the source leaves the water only if it meets the surface at an angle of incidence smaller than the critical angle $θ$:

$\dfrac{4}{3}\sin θ=1\Rightarrow \sin θ=\dfrac{3}{4},\cos θ=\dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{4}$


[IMG]

So the escaping light fills a cone of half-angle $θ$ about the vertical through the source. The source emits equally in all directions, so the escaping fraction equals the area this cone cuts on a sphere of radius $R$ centred on the source, divided by $4πR^{2}$. That area is a spherical cap of height $h=R-R\cos θ$, of area $2πRh$:

$\text{fraction}=\dfrac{2πR^{2}(1-\cos θ)}{4πR^{2}}=\dfrac{1-\cos θ}{2}=\dfrac{4-\sqrt{7}}{8}$

$\dfrac{4-2.646}{8}\approx 0.17=17%$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:

Mean free time, t = $\frac{λ}{v}$

Also v $\propto$ $\sqrt{\frac{T}{M}}$

$\therefore$ t $\propto$ $\frac{\sqrt{M}}{d^{2}}$

$\frac{t_{Ar}}{t_{Xe}}$ = $\frac{d_{Xe}^{2}}{d_{Ar}^{2}}\times \sqrt{\frac{M_{Ar}}{M_{Xe}}}$

= $\left (\frac{0.1}{0.07}\right )^{2}\times \sqrt{\frac{40}{140}}$

= 1.09

$\therefore$ Nearest possible answer is 1.83.

text:
A particle of mass m is projected with a speed
u from the ground at an angle
$θ=\frac{π}{3}$ w.r.t.
horizontal (x-axis). When it has reached its
maximum height, it collides completely
inelastically with another particle of the same
mass and velocity $u\hat{i}$ . The horizontal distance
covered by the combined mass before reaching
the ground is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By momentum conservation,

$\frac{mu}{2}$ + mu = 2mV

$\Rightarrow$ V = $\frac{3u}{4}$

$H_{\max } =$ $\frac{u^{2}\sin ^{2}60^{\circ }}{2g}$ = $\frac{u^{2}\times \frac{3}{4}}{2g}$ = $\frac{3u^{2}}{8g}$

Time taken = $\sqrt{\frac{2H_{\max }}{g}}$ = $\sqrt{\frac{2}{g}\times \frac{3u^{2}}{8g}}$ = $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\frac{u}{g}$

Horizontal distance traveled = Vt

= $\frac{3u}{4}.\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\frac{u}{g}$ = $\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{8}\frac{u^{2}}{g}$

text:
Starting at temperature 300 K, one mole of an

ideal diatomic gas ($γ$ = 1.4) is first compressed

adiabatically from volume $V_{1}$ to $V_{2} =$ $\frac{V_{1}}{16}$. It is

then allowed to expand isobarically to volume
$2V_{2}$. If all the processes are the quasi-static then

the final temperature of the gas (in $^{o}K)$ is (to
the nearest integer$) _____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the adiabatic compression of the diatomic gas ($γ=1.4$), $TV^{γ-1}$ stays constant:

$T_{2}=T_{1}\left (\dfrac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}\right )^{γ-1}=300\times 16^{0.4}$

$16^{0.4}=2^{1.6}=2\times 2^{0.6}\approx 2\times 1.515=3.03$

$T_{2}\approx 300\times 3.03=909\text{K}$

In the isobaric expansion $V\propto T$, so doubling the volume from $V_{2}$ to $2V_{2}$ doubles the temperature:

$T_{f}=2T_{2}\approx 2\times 909=1818\text{K}$

Hence, the answer is 1818.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot

text:
The circuit shown below is working as a 8 V
dc regulated voltage source. When 12 V is used
as input, the power dissipated (in mW) in each
diode is; (considering both zener diodes are
identical$) _________$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The two identical Zener diodes are in series across the regulated 8 V output, so each is in breakdown with

$V_{Z}=\dfrac{8}{2}=4\text{V}$

The remaining $12-8=4\text{V}$ drops across the two $200\Omega$ resistors in series, so the current is

$I=\dfrac{12-8}{200+200}=10^{-2}\text{A}=10\text{mA}$

No load is connected at the output, so this whole current passes through both diodes. Power dissipated in each diode:

$P=V_{Z}I=4\times 10^{-2}\text{W}=40\text{mW}$

Hence, the answer is 40.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Evening Slot
